term: linear per se series (at most one immediate per se cause)
definition: `AtMostOneImmediateCause R`: whenever y and z both R-relate to x, y = z. Each being has at most one immediate per se cause, as in the stone–stick–hand series.
note: An analyst's condition used only as an antecedent of GROUNDING-WITH-UNIQUE-CAUSE-YIELDS-REGRESS-READING; GROUNDING-WITHOUT-UNIQUE-CAUSE-ALLOWS-REGRESS shows it cannot simply be dropped. No source claim says that every per se series is linear; ST I q.2 a.3 only gives a linear example.
